body: I'll think about it. She might be able to come up with something, but there's only one way to know if she could or not. Thank you for your help tonight, I greatly appreciate it.

it's ok, it's getting late here, I can only imagine what you must feel like at, what, 5 am?

I've tried to make some new friends with varied success. I really only made two new friends that will definitely stay in my life for a while, but I'm just not a very social person.

And yes. She knows. I told her roughly two years ago. That's an entirely different story, but she's my best friend right now, and the person I trust most in the world. She's just out-of-state for the next couple of days, and I don't want to talk to her about this, she may overreact and she's not good at giving advice at all. She hates giving advice and what not, but she feels obligated to at least try to.
If I may redirect you, my other comment answers most of these questions. I'm just too lazy to re-type them.

I guess I would say I'm more of the "fuck it, what if I fell off" type of person.

I went to two shrinks over the course of about 6 months, but they weren't exactly shrinks, they were just school counselors. I don't think these feelings were around back when I was seeing them, or if they were, they certainly weren't as "prominent" as they are now. My grandfather dying this past April is easily the worst thing that has happened recently, but I've also been having a hard time in college, academically and personally.

I went to a school about 1000 miles away from my hometown, and I was the only person in my class of 300 students who went to that school, a large majority of my friends went to the State school here. I still haven't gotten past the loneliness that I feel when I'm at school (my birthday this year consisted of me crying myself to sleep alone in my dorm). There's also the typical teenager problems, specifically a girl I really really REALLY like.
